name: Unit 8200

summary.text: Unit 8200 is the Israel Defense Forces' signals-intelligence unit, often compared to the U.S. National Security Agency. Its veterans have founded or led many Israeli technology companies: Check Point co-founder Gil Shwed, CyberArk's Udi Mokady and Palo Alto Networks' Nir Zuk served in the unit, Wiz founder Assaf Rappaport is a former 8200 officer, and Nadav Zafrir, who commanded the unit from 2009 to 2013, co-founded the cybersecurity company-builder Team8 in 2014 with two other 8200 veterans.

facts.claim: Nadav Zafrir commanded Israel Defense Forces Unit 8200, described as the equivalent of the NSA, from 2009 to 2013, and in 2014 established Team8 with co-founders Israel Grimberg and Liran Grinberg, also Unit 8200 veterans.
facts.quote: Zafrir was commander of the Israel Defense Forces Unit 8200 (the equivalent of the NSA) from 2009 to 2013, and in 2014 established Team8 with co-founders Israel Grimberg and Liran Grinberg (also Unit 8200 veterans).

sources.title: Nadav Zafrir: Decorated soldier turned cyber entrepreneur

facts.claim: Team8 operates as a company builder that researches and validates ideas before making an initial investment in exchange for 50 percent of the equity; CNBC described it as part think tank, part incubator and part venture-creation foundry. Illusive Networks was one of its spinouts, and Intel joined its syndicate in 2017.
facts.quote: it gets an initial investment from Team8 in exchange for 50% of the equity

sources.title: Co-founder of Team8: Success requires that the stars align for you. We know how to align them
Intel Joins Team8 Cybersecurity Syndicate, Collaborates With Illusive Networks

facts.claim: Gil Shwed, who co-founded Check Point, was a member of Unit 8200, as were Udi Mokady of CyberArk and Nir Zuk of Palo Alto Networks. The Christian Science Monitor reported in 2014 that Shwed spent four years in the unit in the late 1980s before founding Check Point.
facts.quote: Gil Shwed, who co-founded Check Point, was a member of Unit 8200, as was Udi Mokady of CyberArk and Nir Zuk of Palo Alto Networks.

sources.title: Cybersecurity unit drives Israeli Internet economy

facts.claim: Forbes wrote in 2015 that entrepreneurs coming out of Unit 8200 had built some of the largest cybersecurity companies in the world, including Check Point and Palo Alto Networks, and in 2016 profiled the unit as Israel's 'secret startup machine'.
facts.quote: Entrepreneurs coming out of Unit 8200 have built some of the largest cyber security companies in the world, including Check Point and Palo Alto Networks.

sources.title: Team8 Brings Together Some Of The Sharpest Cyber-Security Minds... The 'What For?' Is TBD

facts.claim: Calcalist reported in 2024 that Alphabet was in advanced talks to buy the cloud-security company Wiz from founder Assaf Rappaport, a former officer in Unit 8200, at a reported value of $23 billion. Calcalist later reported that a Unit 8200 veteran who was among Wiz's first employees went on to co-found Frame Security, and described Wiz's eventual $32 billion acquisition by Google.
facts.quote: founder Assaf Rappaport, a former officer from the famed 8200 military unit

sources.title: Alphabet in advanced talks to buy Wiz
Former Wiz and Team8 executives raise $50 million for cyber startup Frame

facts.claim: Calcalist reported that Talon Cyber Security was co-founded by Ofer Ben-Noon and Ohad Bobrov, both Unit 8200 alumni; Ben-Noon had earlier founded the automotive cybersecurity company Argus, sold to Continental in 2017.
facts.quote: Ben-Noon founded Argus, the global leader in automotive cybersecurity, which was sold to Continental in 2017

openQuestions: Unit 8200 appears in the site's approved web data but not in the entity index; no page text makes a specific claim about it to test.
Claims that NSO Group's founders served in Unit 8200 came only from a Substack post and were not recorded.
Estimates such as 'more than 1,000 companies founded by 8200 veterans' or '80% of Israeli cybersecurity companies' appeared only in blogs or unsourced research notes and were not recorded.
A Wall Street Journal report that at least five U.S.-listed companies started by 8200 alumni are worth around $160 billion was seen only via a secondary blog summary.
Which of Wiz's four co-founders served in Unit 8200, beyond Rappaport, was not confirmed from Calcalist or Times of Israel.
